messages.subject: Linear Discriminant Analysis in R
parts:
Hi,

I am trying to repeat this SPSS data analysis example (http://www.ats.ucla.edu/stat/spss/dae/discrim.htm) in R.

I used this script to generate the graph:
require(MASS)
require(ggplot2)

rawx <-read.csv("C:/Users/Asher_dell/Desktop/discrim_csv.csv")
rawx.lda<-lda(JOB ~ OUTDOOR + SOCIAL+  CONSERVATIVE+ JID, data = rawx )
datPred<-data.frame(JOB=predict(rawx.lda)$class,predict(rawx.lda)$x)

p1<-ggplot(datPred, aes(x=LD1, y=LD2) ) + geom_point( size = 4, aes(color = JOB))
p1<-p1 +   annotate("text", x = -4.5, y = 3.5, label = "A", ,size=10)
p1

Therfore, I have two questions:
- My graph scales are different than the SPSS one, why?
- How can I calculate and add the group centroids?

Thanks a lot in advance.

P.S.
I exported the csv using SPSS.

messages.subject: Re: [Israel RUG] Linear Discriminant Analysis in R
parts:
(1) Please try to post reproducible example. We don't have your csv file you see.
Maybe try:
library(foreign)
read.spss('http://www.ats.ucla.edu/stat/data/discrim.sav')
data<- read.spss('http://www.ats.ucla.edu/stat/data/discrim.sav')
rawx<- as.data.frame(data)

(2) The scales are due to different defaults between ggplot2 and SPSS. Try +xlim() +ylim()  to change ggplot's behaviour.

(3) Not claiming this is the easiest way:
col.ind<- names(rawx)!="JOB"
centers<- predict(rawx.lda, 
        newdata=data.frame(sapply(rawx[col.ind], function(x) tapply(x, rawx$JOB, mean))))$x
p2<-p1 + geom_point(data=as.data.frame(centers), aes(x=centers[,1], y=centers[,2]), size=5)
p2
